newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: National law defines employed and self-employed.
newsitem.headline: National law defines employed and self-employed.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday member state definitions of employment and self-employment activities are to be applied to the Community legislation on social security schemes for migrant workers.
The court noted that in the area of social security on migrant workers, the treaty calls for the coordination of member state schemes, but not harmonization.

Under French and Belgian law, the definition of employed or self-employed worker is distinguished by a relationship of subordination. "A person who performs services for and under the authority of another person is considered employed," the court said.

Belgium wants to collect social security contributions from a French national, Claude Hervein, who resides in France, but who sits on the boards of various companies based in Belgium. Belgium argues that although the French national is designated as employed in France and subject to contributions as an employee there, he should still be subject to self-employment contribution in Belgium, under Belgian law.

Hervein argues that he should not be subject to the Belgian scheme because even though he pays in France as an employee, he is in fact self-employed there and that Community law says that aN individual, self-employed in more than one member state, should pay social security only in the member state where he resides.
The court said the determination of Hervein's status as employee or self-employed must be determined under respective member state law.
"Social security for migrant workers - Determination of the legiaslation applicable - Definition of employed and self-employed"
Reference by the Tribunal du Travail, Tournai, Belgium for a preliminary ruling between
Institut National d'Assurance Sociales pour Travailleurs Independants (Inasti)

on the interpretation of article 14a(2) of regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of the Council of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 (OJ 1983 L 230, p. 5)

For the purposes of articles 14a and 14c regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of the Council of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983, "employment" and "self-employment" should be understood to be the activities which are regarded as such for the purposes of the social security legislation of the member staTe in whose territory those activities are pursued.
